Tabularius 0.2.0 is the second public release of an open-source (MIT) platform that opens and hosts FileMaker `.fmp12` files: it reads a file, converts it once into a SQLite store beside the original (which is left as it was), and serves it through a REST API shaped like the FileMaker Data API, a web client with a design mode, a script engine, a calculation engine and a built-in MCP server for AI tools. It is for all FileMaker developers and solutions, and is not affiliated with Claris.

This is still early software. Keep your original file and a backup, check the conversion report, and read **What does not carry over** below before you rely on a hosted file. While the major number is 0, a minor version may change what is not written down as staying put (`docs/versioning.md`); **Before you upgrade** lists what this one changes for an existing setup.

## What is new since 0.1.0

- **A CRM showcase.** `tabularius demo --starter crm-showcase` hosts a made-up sales app on this computer only: classic layouts (an Account 360 form with portals, a Deals form with quote lines), five modern HTML pages (Today, Sales dashboard, Account timeline, Pipeline board, Connect), scripts, calculations, a won-deal automation and four accounts whose privilege sets show only a rep's own deals. The five pages share one design: headline tiles, a quota ring that shows pace against the quarter, revenue columns, a funnel, a leaderboard, avatars, stage pills, loading and empty states, and a dark mode. The Account timeline has an account picker, a profile card and filters. `--full` adds the sign-ins, a read-only SQL port and a read-only token for an AI app; `--ai` turns on the demo's assistant when you bring your own key. All of its data is invented. `docs/showcase-crm.md` walks through it.
- **Files and folders the server writes or reads are checked for planted links, hard links and pipes.** The credential files (admin password, the MCP token, the connections key, the TLS pair and the CA key, the Vault key), the hosted-file record, command-line export folders and write-back files, plug-in packages, backup sets and their logs, the outbox, inbound-hook call logs and standby copies are read and written only when they are what they should be: owned by the account that runs the server, a plain file with one name, and private. A refusal says which file and why, without showing the path to a remote caller.
- **More of what an administrator does is in the security log.** Restores, ended sessions, server-wide settings (session timeout, new-user block, notifications, backup folder), admin passkeys, schedules, inbound hooks and webhooks (additions, changes and removals, without secrets or full URLs), and backup destination changes now leave a row in the file's security log or the Admin log, with the way in and address. Changes made through the Admin API (blocking new users, importing or deleting a TLS certificate, disconnecting a client) leave the same rows as the console. `ADMIN.md` lists the event kinds.
- **Standby.** A standby refuses a primary address that is unsafe and never follows a redirect, and a primary at `http://` on another computer is refused unless `tabularius standby` is given `--allow-plain-http`.
- **Agent write proposals respect the caller's privileges.** A change an AI agent proposes is approved within the privileges and ceiling of the token it came from.
- **Cluster mode.** Messages between the front process and its workers are checked at both ends, and a worker that cannot open a file reports it to the leader, so the admin status and console show why.
- **Settings are read strictly.** Invalid numeric server and store settings stop `tabularius serve` with a message that names the setting, instead of quietly changing meaning.
- **SQL and calculations.** `EXTRACT(SECOND ...)` gives fractional seconds; `OFFSET` and `FETCH FIRST` accept parameters; 64-bit integer results keep every digit; date arithmetic outside years 0001 to 9999 is an error; `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT` and `DISTINCT` parse as they should and `ALL` is refused by name; `Ceiling`, `Floor`, `Factorial`, `Combination`, exact square roots and large exponent literals keep their exact digits; `Proper` handles combining marks; years below 1000 are written with four digits; a field index sorts text by its own index language; number fields keep non-decimal text instead of changing it, and an import flags it. Excel round trips keep negative and long durations.
- **Web client and admin console.** Form controls in Design mode and the admin console have names a screen reader speaks; a lost connection or a reply that is not JSON is explained in a sentence; the light palette is darker where the contrast was too low. Empty, error and failed-start messages on the stand-alone pages, the web client and the admin console's panels are announced to screen readers, and relationship lines in Design mode can be reached and selected from the keyboard. Show All Records, Show Omitted Only and Perform Quick Find keep the found set's sort.
- **Notification email addresses stay out of the server log.** A failed send, and the mail server's answer to it, are logged with the address's domain only.
- **Redo works after Undo removes a record's only uncommitted change.**
- **The fault log hides folder names.** A folder in a path, including Windows long paths and names with spaces or dots, is hidden before a fault is written.
- **Documentation.** The help text, the runbook, the moving-in guide, the connecting guide and the figures in `docs/features.md` and `ADMIN.md` are now run or checked by tests against the program.

## Before you upgrade

`docs/upgrading.md`, "Changes that can affect existing use", has the whole list. The ones most likely to matter:

- **A server that was started with a bad setting now refuses to start** and says which one: an invalid whole number in any numeric `TABULARIUS_*` setting, a container-link lifetime over 3600 seconds, a secret set but empty (`TABULARIUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${KEY:-}` in a Compose file with `KEY` unset hits this) and a variable that is a near miss of a secret's name. Check your service definition and Compose file first.
- **A standby on a plain `http://` primary on another computer needs `--allow-plain-http`.** `TABULARIUS_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP` does not lift this one, so the Docker image no longer turns the refusal off by accident.
- **A file the server wrote or reads that is a link, has other links, a pipe or the wrong owner or mode is now refused** where it used to be followed. If a service account was changed over time, check that it owns its hosted folder and its credential files.
- **A backup set that is a symlink is ignored**, and a symlinked previous manifest makes the next backup a full copy (it says why).
- **The admin console reads only its `__Host-` cookie over HTTPS.** Over HTTPS it ignores a cookie with the plain name, so a script that sends the plain name is refused (401) and must send the `__Host-` name or sign in again. A person signed in over HTTPS signs in once more after the upgrade.
- **Command-line tools stop on an option they do not know or one with no value**, and on a port, limit or address that is not valid, instead of running without it. A script that passed a mistyped option and got an answer anyway will now fail, which is the point.
- **A checkout made before `v0.1.0` cannot update**, because the history was rewritten once for the first release. `docs/upgrading.md` has the two commands; the single-file program is not affected.

## Install

On macOS or Linux (arm64 or x64), one command installs the single-file program: no Node, nothing else.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/MacBookM5CoderMax/OpenSourceFilemaker/releases/latest/download/get.sh | sh
tabularius demo
```

`tabularius demo` hosts a small sample app on this computer only, opens it in your browser with a one-time password for `Admin`, and deletes everything when you press Ctrl-C. To host your own file, follow `QUICKSTART.md`: run `tabularius`, then drop the file on the page. To upgrade a single-file install, run the same command again; a checkout or a `~/.openhbam/app` install updates with `tabularius upgrade`.

You can also download a program from the files below. Check it with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` (`shasum -a 256 -c` on macOS) and make it runnable with `chmod +x`. A file saved by a browser is quarantined by macOS; clear that with `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <file>`.

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `tabularius-0.2.0-macos-arm64` |
| macOS, Intel | `tabularius-0.2.0-macos-x64` |
| Linux, x64 | `tabularius-0.2.0-linux-x64` |
| Linux, arm64 | `tabularius-0.2.0-linux-arm64` |
| Windows | `tabularius-0.2.0-windows-x64.exe`, only if it is listed below (see "Windows") |

The Linux programs need glibc (not Alpine). `QUICKSTART.md` covers the other ways to install: from a checkout, with Docker, and as a service. Each program has a software bill of materials (`*.sbom.cdx.json`), and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` carries the licence texts of what is inside.

## What it does

- **Reads `.fmp12` files**: tables, fields, relationships, layouts, scripts, value lists, custom functions, accounts, privilege sets, records and container files, including files that use Encryption at Rest when given their passphrase.
- **Hosts them**: point the server at a folder; each file is converted once into its own SQLite database. Accounts and privilege sets come with the file and every way in enforces them.
- **A Data API-shaped REST API.** A conformance suite checks the responses against Claris's published Data API guide, and `docs/data-api-compatibility.md` lists every endpoint, field, header and error code as supported, partial or missing. It is shaped like the FileMaker Data API, not a drop-in copy.
- **Calculations and scripts** run on the server, from buttons, triggers, schedules, the Data API and MCP, with a debugger that works on a scratch copy and can step backwards.
- **A web client with a design mode.** It draws existing layouts, lets you change tables, layouts, calculations and scripts, and lets you build new layouts in HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
- **A built-in MCP server** for AI tools: explore a solution, find and edit records, explain why a field holds a value, and say what a rename or delete would break before it happens, always as the signed-in account and within its privileges. See `docs/connect-ai.md`.
- **Script network access is supported**: Insert from URL, web connections, Send Mail and plug-in network calls work, and are on by default for a hosted file. They start off for `tabularius demo` and for a file just converted from a `.fmp12`, so a copy you are only testing cannot call outside services or email real people. The web client says so at the top of the window, and a step that needs the network stops with a message that names the step and says an administrator turns it on from the admin console's Files page (the **Script network** button for each file, or start the server with `--allow-script-network` for all of them).
- **Self-hosted**: passkeys, single sign-on, daily online backups with verification, point-in-time restore, a standby server, SQL and PostgreSQL access for BI tools, and an admin console.
- **No telemetry, analytics, crash reports or update check.** A server started with no options connects to nothing but this computer (`docs/privacy.md`).

## What does not carry over

- **People use a browser.** There is no FileMaker Pro or FileMaker Go client for a file hosted here.
- **Passwords.** An account whose FileMaker password is empty keeps working, from the server's own computer. Every other account needs a new password (`tabularius passwd`).
- **FileMaker plug-ins are never loaded.** A few BaseElements and MBS functions run as built-in code; any other FileMaker plug-in call gives "?" and error 3. A Tabularius plug-in (JavaScript or WebAssembly) that replaces one runs in a sandbox once an administrator turns it on for a file (`docs/writing-a-plugin.md`).
- **Scripts run on the server.** Steps that need a screen or a person at FileMaker Pro are skipped or give error 3.
- **The store is not the `.fmp12`.** Changes made here can't be written back into a `.fmp12`. `tabularius exit-bundle` writes the whole file to a folder any tool can read; that copy is plaintext, so keep it private.
- **Some conversions need a second look**: Go to Related Record options and Import Records modes are not read from a converted file and must be set again in the script editor; Save a Copy as never makes a `.fmp12`.
- **Recursion depth.** A custom function can recurse 10,000 calls deep in any shape, and deeper nesting gives a clean error rather than a crash. FileMaker allows 50,000 calls for tail recursion, so a solution that relies on that will stop sooner here.
- **Some security detail is flattened**: per-layout, per-value-list and per-script privileges come over at the privilege set's overall level. Review your privilege sets before people sign in.

`tabularius report <folder>` shows what in your file won't work yet. `docs/known-differences.md` is the one list of everything that differs from FileMaker or isn't settled, and `docs/moving-a-solution.md` walks through moving a file.

## Security

The server listens on this computer only until you say otherwise, refuses to listen on the network without HTTPS unless you allow plain HTTP, has no anonymous access, requires a password of at least 12 characters, locks an account after repeated wrong passwords, and gives every API, AI-app and provisioning token an expiry. The AI connector (`/mcp`) needs a credential from everyone, this computer included. `docs/security-defaults.md` lists every default, what changes it and what goes wrong if you change it, and a test checks each row against a running server.

A file that arrives in the hosted folder after the first start, or a `.fmp12` the server converts from it, is **held**: people can read it, but it runs no scripts, schedules, automations, digests or inbound hooks, and no connection is handed to it, until an administrator presses **Approve** next to it on the admin console's Files page. The record of what was approved is a plain local file that anyone who can write to the hosted folder can edit; read `docs/security-defaults.md` before putting the server on a network.

Report a vulnerability privately, as `SECURITY.md` says (on the repository: Security, then Report a vulnerability). Tabularius is looked after by volunteers; there is no response-time commitment.

## Windows

Windows is the least tested system. The release build, the service install check and the test suite run on Windows in CI, and the 0.1.0 program was downloaded and run (`--version`, `demo`, sign-in, Ctrl-C) on a GitHub-hosted Windows machine, but a double-click install and a browser sign-in on a Windows desktop have not been tried, and `docs/audits/audit-windows.md` and `docs/release-builds.md` say so. The program is **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": choose More info, then Run anyway. The Windows program is attached only when it built and passed its check for this release; if it is not in the list below, use the checkout install in `QUICKSTART.md`.

## Versions

This is 0.2.0. While the major number is 0, a minor version may change anything not written down as staying put; `docs/versioning.md` says what stays put (commands, the FileMaker-shaped routes, error codes, hosted files, settings) and what is tested where.
